problems_addressed.specific_problem: High rate of deals falling through after going under contract
problems_addressed.solution_summary: Implement the 30-day grip system to maintain client confidence and manage the deal actively through regular communication.

target_avatars.relevance: This episode addresses the common issue of deals falling apart, which many intermediate agents face.
target_avatars.key_takeaway: Proactively manage client relationships and expectations during the escrow period to prevent deal cancellations.

clip_worthy_moments.quote: You call your client and tell them you called the lender. Going first is the entire thing.
clip_worthy_moments.why_clipworthy: This highlights a proactive approach to client management that can prevent deal fall-throughs.
clip_worthy_moments.suggested_hook: Why going first can save your real estate deals.

key_tactics.context: Call your client within 24 hours of mutual acceptance to outline the next 30 days and set expectations.
Every Tuesday, check in with all parties involved in the deal to ensure everything is on track.
Proactively address potential deal-breaking issues during key moments like inspection, appraisal, and clear to close.

quotable_insights: The deal you lose in escrow is actually the most expensive deal you'll ever lose.

resources_mentioned.name: Redfin's June report
resources_mentioned.context: Used to provide data on the percentage of home sale agreements that fell through.

episode_summary: In this episode, D.J. Paris discusses the high rate of real estate deals falling through after going under contract and introduces the '30-day grip' system to address this issue. He emphasizes the importance of proactive communication and client management during the escrow period to maintain client confidence and prevent cancellations.
